intro: Essaouira is a walled port on Morocco's Atlantic coast, its medina a grid of whitewashed lanes inside eighteenth-century ramparts. In the courtyard of a café there grows an ombu, a tree of the South American pampas, whose trunk spreads over the ground in a broad smooth dome under a crown that fills the whole courtyard. A reader sent us its photograph and calls it the oldest tree in Morocco.

trees.story:
"Oldest tree in Morocco inside the ombu cafe," wrote the reader who sent this photograph from the medina of Essaouira.

The tree is an ombu, Phytolacca dioica, a native of the South American pampas, and the photograph shows why people stop for one. Its trunk does not so much rise from the ground as pour out over it, a broad smooth dome of root and wood ringed by a low rope rail. Out of that dome a dozen grey stems climb into a crown that fills the whole courtyard and leans over the whitewashed walls, and the café's tables stand around its edge in the shade.

The reader puts it at about 250 years old and its trunk at some ten metres round. Neither figure comes from a register or a measurement we have seen, so read them as theirs, and whether it is truly the oldest tree in Morocco we cannot say. If you know its history, or who planted it, tell us here.

It grows inside a café, so the way to see it is to sit down under it and order a mint tea.
trees.how_to_recognise: Fills a walled café courtyard in the medina: a broad smooth dome of trunk and root behind a low rope rail, a dozen grey stems rising from it into a crown over the tables.
trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-16 session: sent by a reader through the app with a GPS fix in the medina of Essaouira (sighting 5784282e), named Phytolacca dioica, age 250 years, girth 1000 cm, note 'Oldest tree in Morocco inside the ombu cafe'. Photograph viewed: the whole tree from its foot, the domed root flare typical of an ombu, many stems, a crown over a walled courtyard with café tables, daylight, colour. Published under the reader-found rule (CLAUDE.md, Hidde 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-21); no register entry within 100 m. A web search found no written source naming the café or the tree; a 2011 Moroccan report of a two-century-old tree in a medina courtyard (communesmaroc.com) may or may not be this one, so it is not cited. Age, girth and the café's name are the reader's. Morocco is out of focus for our own research only, never for a reader's tree.
